entries.content: (e-0) (The title of this book, 'Jermiah'), The name may mean, 'Jah is exalted.' Compare the large use made of the name Jehovah in this book; it occurs about 700 times. Adonai Jehovah 14 times.
almond-tree. (e-23) Derived from a word meaning, 'watchful' or 'vigilant,' as ver. 12; ch. 31.28; Num. 17.8; Dan. 9.14.
land, (a-8) Heb. 'land of Carmel;' as ch. 4.26.
transgressed (b-20) Or 'rebelled.' so ver. 29; chs. 3.13; 33.8. see Isa. 1.2.
Tahapanes (c-7) See Notes, Isa. 19.13; 30.4; Jer. 44.1. on (d-10) Others, 'have broken.'
these. (a-29) Or '... innocent poor; I have not found it by violently breaking in [i.e. into secret places], but upon all these.' For sense see Ex. 22.2,3.
lovers; (c-39) Strictly, 'companions,' 'friends.' see Cant. 5.16, and Note, Cant. 1.9.
heights (d-7) Or 'high places,' strictly, 'bare hills.' see Isa. 41.18; 49.9. so ver. 21; ch. 4.11, &c.
determined. (a-26) Or 'hast known how to carry them out.' lit. 'thou prevailest,' Gen. 32.28.
dark (c-23) Lit. 'cause my face to fall.'
thither (d-20) Lit. 'hast scattered thy ways.' strangers (e-23) i.e. false gods.
mind, (f-38) Or 'rise in the heart.' done (g-53) Or 'made,' if the ark be meant.
of (i-27) Or 'the most lovely inheritance of.' me. (k-46) Lit. 'from after me.'
sore; (a-16) As 'writhing,' Ps. 55.4, and cf. Prov. 23.35.
God. (d-18) Or 'no gods,' as ch. 2.11. satiated (e-21) Some read 'adjured.'
end; (f-13) Or 'a consumption;' ch. 4.27. battlements, (g-17) Some, referring it to a vine, read 'tendrils' or 'shoots.'
prosper; (a-26) Or 'that they might bring them through.'
signal (c-24) Perhaps 'of fire.' see Judg. 20.38. Beth-haccerem; (d-26) i.e. the vineyard house. destruction. (e-37) Or 'breach,' as ver. 14; ch. 8.21.
out (a-18) others 'I will pour it out.'
breach (b-6) Or 'wound.' of (c-10) Many omit 'the daughter of,' but see ch. 8.11.
that (d-4) Or 'They have come to shame because.' so in ch. 8.12.
them. (e-12) Or 'nations, and know the testimony that is among them.'
cane (f-15) As 'sweet myrtle,' Ex. 30.23; 'calamus,' Cant. 4.14; 'cane,' Isa. 43.24.

burned, (a-4) * i.e. so that the current of air, needed to cause the lead to carry off the dross, ceased, leaving unrefined (reprobate) silver. It might read 'the bellows puff.' fire; (b-11) Others, 'out of their fire [cometh] lead.'
people; (a-23) Lit. 'I will be to you for God, and ye shall be to me for people.'
place. (d-38) Or 'for want of another place;' and so ch. 19.11.
silent (c-20) Or 'let us perish.' silence, (d-30) Or 'made us to perish.' gall (e-36) See Ps. 69.21.
steeds, (f-22) Lit. 'mighty ones.' see Judg. 5.22; Ps. 22.12. contains, (g-33) Lit. 'all its fulness.'
breach (a-4) Or 'crushing,' or 'destruction' as ch. 6.1. The word is the same in ver. 11 and ch. 6.14, and as the verb 'crushed' in this verse, and 'ruin,' Lam. 2.11.
neighbour, (b-9) Or 'friend,' as ver. 4. see ch. 3.1.
neighbour (b-16) Or 'friend,' as ver. 4. see ch. 3.1.
stock. (e-16) Or 'wood is an instruction of vanity.'
fortress. (d-13) Or 'thou that dwellest in the straitness' (i.e. 'distress') or 'in the siege.'
lamb (d-7) Or 'like a lamb, an ox.'
security, (b-30) Or 'if thou confidest in a land of peace.'
prey; (c-11) According to others 'as a greedy hyena.'
south (a-5) Negeb. so chs. 17.26; 32.44. see Gen. 12.9.
thee? (b-22) Or 'What wilt thou say, when he shall appoint as chief over thee those whom thou hast taught to be thy familiars?'
ones (d-7) Or 'their menials,' as also ch. 48.4.
cease; (a-21) Or 'Mine eyes run down with tears, night and day, and they cease not.'
not. (b-42) Or 'wander about in the land, and they know not [what to do].'
HE, (d-23) Or 'thou, the Same.' see Deut. 32.39.
name, (b-29) Lit. 'thy name is called upon me.'
assembly (c-6) Elsewhere 'secret council.' mockers, (d-9) Or 'them that make merry,' as. ch. 31.4.
vile, (e-28) Same word as 'profligate,' Deut. 21.20; 'vile,' Lam. 1.11.
go (a-7) Or 'on thine own account thou shalt leave.' Some suppose a reference to Deut. 15.2.
heath (c-7) Or 'a denuded (or, forlorn) [man];' as ch. 48.6.
lowland, (a-25) The Shephelah. see Deut. 1.7. south, (b-33) The Negeb, Gen. 12.9. see chs. 13.19 and 32.44.
clay, (c-10) Another reading is found in many MSS., 'that he made of clay was spoiled.'
field? (a-12) It may be translated, 'Shall the snow of Lebanon be left which cometh from the rock of the field?' up? (b-23) Or 'be abandoned.'
me. (f-12) Or 'their deadly counsel against me '
void (a-5) Or 'empty,' alluding to the empty 'earthen flagon' of ver. 1.
Magor-missabib. (a-31) Meaning, 'Terror on every side,' as ver. 10; chs. 6.25; 46.5; 49.29; Ps. 31.13; and Lam. 2.22.
prospered. (d-29) Or 'not dealt wisely.' see ch. 10.21.
plain, (c-14) Mishor, generally applied to the table-land of Moab; here, Jerusalem.
But (f-1) Lit. 'For.' extortion, (g-11) Or 'over-reaching,' as 'covetousness,' Ex. 18.21.
Coniah (b-7) Called Jeconiah in chs. 24.1; 28.4; 29.2; 1Chron. 3, &c. Jehoiachin in ch. 52.31 and 2Kings.
Branch, (e-15) Strictly, 'Sprout.' see ch. 33.15; Isa. 4.2; Zech. 3.8; 6.12. wisely, (f-23) Or 'and prosper,' as ch. 20.11. See Note, Prov. 1.3, sachal. land. (g-32) Or 'earth.'
broken; (h-9) Or 'My heart is broken for the prophets.'
vanity; (b-22) Or 'befool you.' see ch. 2.5, and 2Kings 17.15.
had (c-10) Or 'counsel, then would they have.'
neighbour. (e-21) Or 'friend.' as vers. 30,35. see ch. 3.1. for (f-29) Or 'through.'
are (b-20) Or 'those whom for good I have,' &c.
also; (a-12) Or 'shall reduce them to servitude, even them.'
Tema, (c-3) Job 22.1; Isa. 21.14. Buz, (d-5) Job 32.2, Buzite. off; (e-16) See ch. 9.26.
Sheshach (f-33) An enigmatical name for Babel, formed by reversing the order of the Hebrew letters. see ch. 51.41, also 51.1, and Note.
dwelling-place, (h-33) Or 'against his fold (pasture).' see ch. 23.3; Isa. 65.10.
Jehoiakim (c-8) Perhaps 'Zedekiah,' unless ver. 3 be wrong.
soothsayers, (b-19) Or, 'those that use auguries,' as Lev. 19.26.
hope. (b-28) Lit. 'a latter end and hope.' ch. 31.17.
end (a-17) See Note, ch. 4.27. guiltless. (b-50) Or 'leave thee wholly unpunished.' see ch. 25.29.
medicines. (d-17) Or 'there are no medicines [nor] healing for thee.'
habitations; (f-18) Or 'tabernacles.' heap; (g-28) Or 'mound.' see Josh. 8.28; 11.13.
prince (h-3) Translated 'excellent,' Ps. 8.1,9; 'mightier,' Ps. 93.4; 'noble ones,' ch. 25.34-36. engageth (i-37) Or 'pledgeth,' as 'surety,' Gen. 44.32.
thee. (a-24) Or 'I have prolonged toward thee my goodness.'
goodness (d-19) Or 'good things,' and see Deut. 6.11.
goodness, (d-20) Or 'good things,' and see Deut. 6.11.
broke, (d-35) Or 'because they broke my covenant.'
mounds, (b-3) i.e. mounds cast up by the besiegers.
good; (b-21) Lit. 'in my doing them good.'
lowland, (c-47) Shephelah. see Deut. 1.7. south. (d-54) Negeb. see ch. 13.19 and Josh. 10.40.
Branch (c-12) Or 'Sprout,' as ch. 23.5. land. (d-29) Or, 'upon the earth.'
fail (e-8) Lit. 'be cut off;' as ch. 35.19.
fail (e-4) Lit. 'be cut off;' as ch. 35.19. burn (f-20) See Notes, Lev. 1.9; 2.2. continually. (g-26) Lit. 'all the days.'
land (b-34) Lit. 'upon the face of the ground.'
supplication (a-8) Lit. 'their supplication will fall.' before (b-9) Lit. 'before the face of.'
Hammelech, (b-9) Or 'son of the king;' one of the royal family. see ch. 38.6.
among (b-20) Some translate 'thence to slip away through.'
dungeon (c-7) Lit. 'house of the pit,' as Ex. 12.29; or 'cistern,' Isa. 36.16. see ch. 41.9 and Gen. 37.20.
dungeon (a-10) As ch. 37.16, and so throughout. Hammelech, (b-16) See Note, ch. 36.26.
friends (a-30) As ch. 20.10, and Ps. 41.9. back. (b-51) Or '[thy friends] have withdrawn from [thee].'
answer; (a-8) Or 'returned.' provisions (b-65) Or 'rations.' As 'allowance,' ch. 52.34; 2Kings 25.30.
pit (a-3) As ch. 37.16. of (b-23) Or 'because of.'
Geruth-Chimham, (a-7) Or 'in the caravanserai (i.e. inn) of Chimham.'
souls, (a-8) Or 'led astray your own souls.'
pillars (b-6) Or 'obelisks.' Beth-shemesh, (c-8) Meaning, 'House (or Temple) of the sun;' hence called by the Greeks Heliopolis. The Egyptian name is On (Gen. 41.45).
wickedness (e-5) Lit. 'wickednesses,' in all this verse.
Phut (b-19) Ethiopia and Libya. Ludim (c-26) Lydians of Africa.
Amon (e-13) An Egyptian idol. No, (f-15) Thebes.
end (a-20) Or 'make a consumption,' see Note, ch. 4.27. guiltless. (b-54) See ch. 30.11.
waste (d-9) Or 'spoil,' as elsewhere. island (e-35) Or 'sea-coast.' see Amos 9.7.
praise (g-2) Or 'exultation.' devised (h-10) A play on words. B'Heshbon hashbu.
shrub (k-9) Or 'a denuded person,' as ch. 17.6.
undone; (f-10) Or 'hath perished.' see Num. 21.29; 'ruined,' Ex. 10.7.
Malcam (g-19) Or 'their king;' but it may be another form of Milcom, the divinity of the Ammonites. see Amos 1.15; 5.26. heir (h-20) Elsewhere 'possessor.'
towns (i-34) Lit. 'daughters;' and so often. him, (a-47) Or 'and Israel shall inherit them that were heirs to him.' see ver. 1.
thee; (c-20) Or 'more than are about thee.'
Bel (b-20) Merodach (b-25) A Babylonian idol. dismayed. (c-27) dismayed. (c-37) Or 'broken in pieces.'
mountains. (d-20) Or 'caused them to go astray on the perverting mountains,' alluding to the idolatrous high places.
hindmost (f-22) Or 'the last,' as Amalek was said to be 'the first.' Num. 24.20.
rebellion, (a-8) Or 'apostasy,' Heb. Merathaim. Some take the word as a symbolic name of Babylon. see ch. 51.1, and Note. visitation; (b-16) Or 'punishment.' Heb. Pekod. see Ezek. 23.23.
one, (c-7) Lit. 'pride,' as ch. 49.16. It is Babylon personified.
one (c-4) Lit. 'pride,' as ch. 49.16. It is Babylon personified.
me, (a-24) Lit. 'the heart of Leb-kamai,' which is perhaps enigmatical for 'the Chaldeans.' see Note, ch. 25.26.
forsaken, (c-5) Lit. 'not in widowhood.' land (d-17) i.e. the land of the Chaldeans.
take (c-4) Lit. 'fill' (i.e. with arm, or body); as 'provideth,' 2Sam. 23.7.
sea, (e-22) i.e. the Euphrates. see Isa. 19.5.
*God (d-25) El, only twice in Jeremiah, here, and ch. 32.18; once in Lam., ch. 3.41.
(c-0) Compare ch. 39.1-10 and 2Kings 25.1, et seq. turrets (d-43) Or 'watch-towers.'
brass; (e-15) Or 'with double chains of bronze.' see ch. 39.7.
bowls, (a-12) Or 'basons,' see Note, 1Kings 7.40. brass (b-21) Or 'copper.'
bowls, (a-9) Or 'basons,' see Note, 1Kings 7.40. censers, (c-6) Or 'fire-pans.'
bases, (d-15) Or 'that were under the bases.'
